title: Traffic Sentience Playbook — Resilience Scenarios (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for a cross-functional approach to canarying and A/B experiments with an explicit focus on resilience and adaptive exposure ("traffic sentience"). The goal is to give stewards and oncall teams a lightweight decision matrix, synthetic scenario tests, and an ops checklist that minimizes blast radius while enabling fast learning.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: Product PMs, release stewards, SRE, observing engineers, solutions engineering, data science (evals).
- Scope: Host-API + Dedicated deployments, but patterns should be applicable to Private with network/region caveats.

High-level assumptions (working):
- We can route by region/model/plan-tier and apply traffic tags at the gateway.
- Token-level telemetry (latency/cost) and per-route quality signals (eval-set pass rates) are available in Console.
- We can fold in fallback model variants automatically.

Core concepts introduced here:
- Traffic Sentience: automated exposure adjustments based on multi-signal heuristics (latency, error rate, quality regressions, cost drift).
- Resilience scenarios: pre-defined synthetic tests that simulate degraded GPUs, KV cache misses, and slow tail latency.
- Steward vs. Operator roles: steward owns hypothesis and business signals; operator owns rollout mechanics and escalation.

Decision matrix (simple):
- Signal types (priority order): safety/regulatory > correctness (eval fail) > errors (5xx) > latency P95 > cost/unit increase > user dropoff.
- Action mapping:
  - safety/regulatory hit -> immediate deactivate cohort, full-page incident + legal alert (sev0).
  - correctness regression (>5% relative) -> pause expansion, revert cohort to previous model, notify PM + ML.
  - sustained error rate (>1% over baseline for 10min) -> throttle + fallback to variant.
  - latency P95 > SLO by 50% -> reduce cohort exposure 10x and enable KV-cache-only mode.
  - cost/unit > budget threshold -> cap max tokens and revert to lower quant profile.

Cohort selection heuristics (novelty):
- Use orthogonal cohort dimensions: geography, device type, request path (e.g., reranker vs. completion), account age.
- Pick cohorts that minimize correlated risk (avoid grouping high-LTV accounts together in the first wave).
- Synthetic seed: hold back ~0.5% of internal traffic (canary pool) seeded from shadow traffic + scripted probes.

Exposure schedule (example):
- Wave 0: internal canary (100% internal traffic, feature-flagged) for 30m with targeted synthetic probes.
- Wave 1: 0.1% external traffic for 1 hour (monitoring sweep).
- Wave 2: 1% external for 4 hours (evaluate).
- Wave 3: 5% for 24 hours with A/B evaluator running.
- Wave 4: progressive ramp to target over days.

Telemetry and queries to predefine (to be added to Console as saved views):
- Per-cohort: request_count, token_count, latency_p50/p95/p99, 5xx_rate, model_eval_pass_rate (per prompt-set), user_accept_rate (product metric).
- Cost signals: cost_per_token, estimated_daily_cost_delta.
- Drift checks: distribution shift on prompt length, user locale, common top-10 intents.

Resilience scenario tests (lab):
- Scenario A: GPU slowdown (introduce 400–800ms tail to one pool) -> expected: traffic-sentience reduces cohort exposure, KV-cache path compensates, end-to-end latency remains acceptable for higher-tier accounts.
- Scenario B: KV cache miss storm (evict KV caches) -> expected: observe token cost jump, latency spike; sentinel to cap tokens and throttle non-priority routes.
- Scenario C: Model quality regression (push bad quant profile) -> evaluator catches >5% drop on golden set -> automated canary rollback.
- Scenario D: Partial region outage -> smart routing should shift traffic to nearest healthy region variant; monitor for user impact.

Synthetic traffic recipes (quick):
- Reranker stress: 80k requests over 10m with 8–12 re-ranks per session.
- Long-horizon completion: 5k requests with 2k token targets to exercise KV cache.
- Edge-case prompts: curated 200 prompt set for hallucination/harm checks.

Ops checklist (pre-rollout):
- [ ] Confirm steward sign-off on hypothesis and exposure plan.
- [ ] Confirm runbook pages linked and pager rotations covered.
- [ ] Baseline metrics snapshot saved (console query IDs).
- [ ] Synthetic probe schedule uploaded and validated.
- [ ] Fallback variants tested (routing + A/B keys).
- [ ] Cost cap thresholds set and verified.
- [ ] Communication: stakeholders notified (GTM, CS, SRE, Legal if needed).

Runbook snippets (what oncall sees):
- Alert: "canary-correctness-drop" -> triage steps: check eval-run dashboard -> if >=5% fail and steady for 15m -> revert to previous model, notify steward, open postmortem.
- Alert: "canary-latency-tail" -> check which pool, run GPU health dashboard, if P95 > 2x SLO -> reduce exposure to 10% of current.

A/B design notes (short):
- Metric hierarchy: primary product metric (user_accept_rate) > model-eval pass rate > latency P95.
- Randomization key: user_id hashed with salt derived from deployment id.
- Minimum detectable effect planning: run power calc for each primary metric; target minimum 1.5–2% uplift for high-traffic experiments.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- How do we encode mixed-signal heuristics in a single ownership config? (steward YAML vs. Console UI?)
- Should cost-driven gates be soft (alerts) or hard (auto-throttle)? Proposal: default soft with per-account hard caps opt-in.
- Integration with Dedicated SLA: what are guaranteed fallbacks when model pool is overloaded?

Experiment/canary templates (scratch):
- template: "canary-basic": {exposure_waves: [internal,0.1,1], metrics: [eval_pass,latency_p95,5xx], rollback_conditions: [eval_drop>5,5xx>1%] }
  - (this is a shorthand sketch for engineers to implement in rollout infra).

Notes to self / to-dos:
- Add Confluence page that maps Console saved views -> alert IDs -> playbook steps. (link CONFLUENCE-ROLL-2042)
- Schedule cross-team dry-run with SRE + PMs for 'Scenario B' (KV miss).
- Draft a short comms template for customer-facing incident that includes fallback activated.

Choppy/friction notes (work-in-progress):
- Need clearer naming conventions for cohorts; current internal names collide with traffic-slice labels in Console.
- Ops UI missing quick revert button tied to fallback variant; file ticket.

References and related artifacts:
- JIRA: JIRA-ROLL-4567 (rollout infra: exposure automation)
